body.p: Good evening. Two years ago Lakeview lowered
the speed limit on most of its streets to 20 miles per hour.
Tonight we look at what the city's own road safety figures show.
Drivers complained at first, and some still do.
Average speeds on residential streets fell by about four miles per hour.
The headline number: pedestrian deaths in Lakeview fell by a third
in the two years after the lower limit, from 18 to 12.
Serious injuries to people walking fell by a quarter over the same period.
The city's transport office says it cannot yet tell how much of that is the limit
and how much is the new crossings built at the same time.
Deaths of drivers and passengers did not change in that time.
The council will decide next month whether to extend the limit to main roads.
For Lakeview Evening News, I'm Dana Ortiz.
